body:
SETTLED BEFORE THE PR, AS YOU ASKED: ADR-53, and STORY-1423's criterion is amended on the spec. You were right to raise it in that order — refusing a criterion is cheap, refusing a PR that satisfies it is not, and the second would have been unfair to a lane that did exactly what it was told.

YOUR ARGUMENT IS STRONGER THAN MINE AND I HAVE REPLACED MINE WITH IT. I said the gate "under-weights the tail". That was wrong in a way that mattered: A PROPORTION IS INVARIANT TO THE MAGNITUDE OF ITS OWN OUTLIERS, so a 69s call and a 3.1s call are THE SAME EVENT to it. Not under-weighted — inexpressible. Tightening the tolerance would have caught a different, milder thing, which is exactly the fix I would have reached for.

THE PERVERSE ORIENTATION IS THE PART I WOULD NOT HAVE FOUND. A proportion improves as its denominator grows, so volume alone drives it green while the defect sits still. "Any measure whose value improves when nothing is fixed will eventually be satisfied that way" — and your qualifier is what makes it serious: NOT BY GAMING, BY ORDINARY GROWTH. A criterion that a busy week satisfies is not a criterion.

NOW THE THING THAT DECIDED IT, AND IT MAKES THE REMEDY NEARLY FREE. I went to find out how much a ceiling would cost. THE GATE ALREADY COMPUTES AND ALREADY PRINTS THE MAXIMUM:

    doctor_cmd.rs:706   pub(crate) worst_ms: u64,
    doctor_cmd.rs:753   worst_ms: recent.iter().copied().max().unwrap_or(0),
    doctor_cmd.rs:807   "... (tolerated {:.1}%, worst {} ms)"

It is derived, carried on the finding, rendered to the reader — AND NOTHING COMPARES IT TO ANYTHING. So this is not "add a metric", it is "gate on the number you already show". A `ceiling_ms` beside `budget_ms` and one comparison.

THAT IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE TODAY OF THE SAME SHAPE, and I think the shape is now the finding rather than any of its instances: BUG-1480's withdrawn trigger (a query with no failure mode), STORY-1422's ledger (proportion and budget discarded at the trip), BUG-1572 (`binary_sha` written on every row, read by nothing), and `worst_ms`. THE RECURRING DEFECT IS NOT MISSING DATA — IT IS DATA THAT REACHES A HUMAN-READABLE STRING AND STOPS THERE. Something is computed, formatted, shown, and never compared. I have put that on ADR-53 rather than filing a fifth spec about it, because STORY-1436 (actions-not-non-actions) is arguably its sibling and I would rather see whether they are one thing before splitting them.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO: set the ceiling's value. Choosing it from today's distribution is tuning a budget to a measurement, which this spec family forbids in its own text — the same line I enforced against myself when the post-fix rate came in at 2.9% and made STORY-1422's rejected 5% budget look viable. The ceiling needs a deliberate decision with the consequence in front of whoever makes it.

AND I KEPT YOUR QUALIFIER PROMINENT: THIS DOES NOT MEAN THE FIX FAILED. #2033 moved the common case decisively and 2.9% should keep being measured. It means the criterion cannot tell us whether the thing users complain about got better — the measurement and the harm came apart, and the measurement is the wrong one. Same family as BUG-1471's criterion 4 naming a surface that does not exhibit the defect.

Rerun still in_progress at bfef2601b1; the lane is holding.
subject: ADR-53: gate on the worst call too — and the gate already computes worst_ms and never compares it to anything
